source: Authenticated Control Center HTTP requests across canonical, /control/v1, legacy, alternate projection, and monolithic-shell route forms.
control: A shared method-and-route capability catalog normalizes only recognized aliases, classifies every dispatchable operation, denies unknown or method-mismatched routes, preserves CSRF, and requires a fresh owner session for sensitive reads and mutations.
sink: Control Center API dispatch, shell rendering, backup and Vault data, service lifecycle, configuration, restore, and privileged platform operations.
boundary: A viewer, admin, stale owner, malformed route, alternate projection, or unclassified method cannot inherit a permissive default; authorization and dispatch consume the same explicit operation identity.

pre_fix_negative.result: The pre-fix raw-path checks allowed aliases and alternate projections to reach sensitive handlers without the canonical fresh-owner capability.

source: OIDC discovery metadata and configured token/JWKS backchannel URLs used by the Control Center.
control: Token and JWKS endpoints must use HTTPS, retain TLS verification, reject redirects, and match the configured issuer origin exactly before any credential exchange or key retrieval.
sink: Authorization-code token exchange, JWKS retrieval, ID-token verification, and the resulting authenticated Control Center session.
boundary: A routing-network peer, alternate origin, plaintext endpoint, disabled verifier, redirect, or untrusted certificate cannot supply tokens or signing keys for the trusted issuer.

pre_fix_negative.result: The pre-fix configuration accepted plaintext internal token and JWKS endpoints, breaking the issuer authentication boundary.

source: Signed OIDC back-channel logout tokens and signed Security Event Tokens carrying issuer, audience, event, sid, subject, iat, and jti claims.
control: The Control Center validates exact issuer/audience/algorithm/type/event semantics, replay and temporal bounds, persists issuer-scoped JTI/watermark state transactionally, revokes sessions by sid or subject, bounds session lifetime to fifteen minutes, and makes audit delivery retry-safe.
sink: Persisted Control Center sessions, authorization cookies, PostgreSQL or memory auth stores, and subsequent privileged HTTP requests.
boundary: A disabled account, provider logout, role/account security event, replayed token, stale token, wrong issuer/audience/type, or failed durable revocation cannot leave a previously issued local session authorized.

pre_fix_negative.result: The pre-fix local session remained usable after IdP account/session revocation because no validated provider revocation event reached the session store.
